title: Mouse Without Borders - Use Service does not work before Windows login after fresh boot

judgment.rationale: The public reproduction and eliminated alternatives support a targeted service-startup investigation. The lightweight plan should verify the service lifecycle and pre-logon listener initialization before any implementation-grade design.
evidence: PowerToys 0.101.2362 Microsoft Store on Windows 11 remote PC; Use Service enabled and service account LocalSystem.
The reporter verified the service exists, binary path, firewall, network, policy, key, and service recreation.
The failure is limited to the first boot before the first user login; after login and on later Win+L lock screens it works.
A diagnostic ZIP is attached and the report references similar issue 29060.
judgment.recommended_action: Design Mouse Without Borders pre-logon service startup

fix_assessment.rationale: A repository change may be applicable to service startup/initialization, but the exact failing branch still needs maintainer-side tracing.

proposed_fixes.title: Start and initialize Mouse Without Borders service before first logon
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Use Service path appears to leave the MWB listener unavailable until the first interactive user session, despite the LocalSystem service being installed and enabled.
plan: Trace service registration/startup and the first-logon initialization boundary for PowerToys.MWB.Service.
Verify whether listener/configuration initialization depends on the per-user runner or an interactive session.
Move only the required listener initialization into the service-safe pre-logon path and retain user-session handoff for settings/UI state.
Add coverage for a fresh boot at the Windows sign-in screen and for later Win+L lock-screen operation.
verification: Reproduce a fresh boot with ports 15100 and 15101 unavailable before login, then verify they are listening and the peer controls the sign-in screen after the fix.
Verify later lock-screen reconnection and normal post-login settings behavior.

confidence.rationale: The first-logon boundary and verified service state strongly implicate lifecycle initialization, but code tracing is needed to confirm whether startup, configuration loading, or listener binding is the missing step.

issue_context.summary: With Mouse Without Borders Use Service enabled, the LocalSystem service is present but ports 15100/15101 are unavailable at the first Windows logon screen after a fresh boot. The service becomes available immediately after the first interactive login, while later lock-screen use works.
known_information: PowerToys 0.101.2362 Microsoft Store on Windows 11 remote PC; Use Service enabled and service account LocalSystem.
The reporter verified the service exists, binary path, firewall, network, policy, key, and service recreation.
The failure is limited to the first boot before the first user login; after login and on later Win+L lock screens it works.
A diagnostic ZIP is attached and the report references similar issue 29060.
inferences: The service may be demand-started without a boot/session trigger that initializes the MWB listener before the first logon.
The existing service may start but defer listener initialization until the per-user PowerToys runner or configuration becomes available.
issue_context.analysis: The public reproduction and eliminated alternatives support a targeted service-startup investigation. The lightweight plan should verify the service lifecycle and pre-logon listener initialization before any implementation-grade design.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete reproduction and all verified eliminations in the report.
Identified the service startup type and first-logon boundary as the primary control-flow discriminator.
Kept issue 29060 as related context, not proof of the same root cause.

actions.label: Design Mouse Without Borders pre-logon service startup
Reproduce Mouse Without Borders pre-logon failure

prerequisites: Windows 11 remote PC with Use Service enabled
Windows 10 peer already running Mouse Without Borders
LAN connectivity and ports 15100/15101 available after login
steps: Enable Use Service while PowerToys is elevated and confirm PowerToys.MWB.Service runs as LocalSystem.
Reboot the Windows 11 remote PC and remain at the first Windows sign-in screen without logging in.
From the Windows 10 peer, attempt to connect and inspect whether TCP ports 15100 and 15101 are listening.
Log in locally and repeat the connection test.
reproduce.expected_result: With Use Service enabled, the listener should be reachable before first logon; the current failure is that both ports become available only after interactive login.
